What the athlete said:
- "What I’d like is for you to build out some variation. Keep it on the 5 day plan. Add abs (core) and anything else like rear deltoids that you feel like are missing. I’d also like to potentially add cardio. I have a pull up bar, lat pulldown, EZ bar, barbell, dumbbells to 75, cables with rope and handles, dip bar, belt squat attachment, bench, and a Peloton."
Your plan from the conversation: Athlete wants more variation while staying on the current 5-day split (Push/Pull/Legs/Upper/Lower), plus added core work, more rear delt/shoulder health work, and some cardio worked in. Program: Strength Block
Athlete: goal strength; level intermediate; equipment full gym; work around nothing.
What the athlete said:
- "Take conventional deadlifts out of my program completely. I just don’t like them."
Your plan from the conversation: Athlete dislikes conventional deadlifts and wants them removed from the program entirely, for the rest of the block. Plan: pull conventional deadlift from any session it appears in and replace with another suitable posterior-chain/pull movement.

On Pull I swapped the rear delt fly for a second biceps movement, so you get barbell curls plus dumbbell hammer curls every pull day. Program: 8-Week Muscle Block
Athlete: goal muscle; level intermediate; equipment pullup, latpulldown, barbell, plates, ezbar, dumbbells, cable, bench, dip, bike; work around nothing.
What the athlete said:
- "I want to get stronger now, not bigger"
Your plan from the conversation: Athlete wants to train for strength, not size. Currently on an 8-Week Muscle Block with hypertrophy rep ranges (8-15 reps, shorter rest). Shift remaining sessions to lower reps (roughly 3-6), heavier loads, and longer rest between sets on the main lifts, keeping the same push/pull/legs split.
